comparisons.reason: Different constructs. Left requires a comment to explicitly concede a valid point in the OP's view and then, later in the same comment, disagree. That is a concession-then-disagreement structure. Right requires a comment to explicitly challenge an underlying assumption or premise of the OP, as opposed to disputing facts or the conclusion. A comment can challenge a premise with no concession, and can concede then dispute facts only. The null rules also differ: left returns null if OP context is missing, while right returns null only if both title and argument are missing.
